site.name: Badger Mine
overview: Badger Mine is a documented historic mine locality in Boulder County, mapped near Jamestown on the Boulder USGS quadrangle.

County archival records identify a Badger mine in Boulder County mining records from the late nineteenth century, while modern Colorado mining records show renewed prospecting activity under the Badger Mine name in 2013.

timeline.text: Boulder County surveyor records preserved by the Carnegie Library for Local History index a Badger mine in the county's historic mining records.
Colorado's Division of Reclamation, Mining and Safety received a hard-rock prospecting notice for a Boulder County project named Badger Mine, filed as NOI P-2013-019.

moreHistory: The mapped mine locality is recorded at approximately 40.10999, -105.35860 and is identified as an inactive fluorine mine in geographic records derived from U.S. Geological Survey mapping.

Historic source indexing and modern locality databases use differing district labels for Badger Mine, so this entry uses the more certain Boulder County and mapped-site identification rather than presenting a disputed historic district label as settled fact. The coordinate is a site-level identification point and not a statement about current access, ownership, or the condition of individual mine workings.
